nodes.label: The Selfless Caregiver
nodes.description: Believing I must bear my mother's decline completely alone.
summary: Carried the burden of caregiving entirely by herself initially.
Felt isolated in the experience of losing her mother.

quotes.text: Like I'm not holding the whole thing by myself.

nodes.label: The Invisible Anger
nodes.description: Holding deep resentment that went unexpressed for years.
summary: Expressed past anger toward her brother at the diner.
Noticed feeling less angry after finally talking.

quotes.text: It made me less angry. Not all the way. But a lot.

nodes.label: Anticipatory Loss
nodes.description: Mourning a mother who is physically present but psychologically slipping away.
summary: Faced the devastating reality of her mother not recognizing her.
Described the experience of ambiguous loss and hundred small goodbyes.

quotes.text: There's just a hundred small goodbyes.

nodes.label: Expressing Pain Burdens Others
nodes.description: Assuming that sharing difficult feelings will cause rejection or conflict.
summary: Feared Daniel would not respond or would push her away when she reached out.
Initially kept her grief hidden to avoid worsening the situation.

quotes.text: He didn't answer for like a whole day, and I was sure I'd made it worse.

nodes.label: Avoiding Hard Feelings
nodes.description: Believing that difficult emotions can and should be numbed away.
summary: Used three to four glasses of wine to escape the pain of her mother not recognizing her.

quotes.text: I don't think wanting to not feel it was crazy.

nodes.label: Walking Before Wine
nodes.description: Using physical movement to help transition and reduce the urge to drink.
summary: Completed four nights of walking instead of drinking.
Found that the walk successfully helped her put the stress down on some nights.

quotes.text: The walk kind of did the thing. The putting-it-down thing.

nodes.label: Reaching Out for Support
nodes.description: Initiating vulnerable conversations with family instead of isolating.
summary: Invited her brother Daniel for coffee to share her needs.
Planned to call Daniel instead of turning to alcohol on hard nights.

quotes.text: I need help, and I need you to hear me.

nodes.label: Numbing with Wine
nodes.description: Drinking alcohol to escape intense emotional pain.
summary: Drank heavily on the worst night when her mother did not recognize her.

quotes.text: And that night I skipped the walk and I had three glasses.

nodes.label: Rest and Restoration
nodes.description: Needing physical and mental downtime to recover from burnout.
summary: Slept eight hours straight after getting her Saturday back.
Experienced the restorative benefit of having unassigned personal time.

quotes.text: I slept eight hours last night. I don't remember the last time that happened.

nodes.label: Connection and Shared Burden
nodes.description: Longing for empathy and partnership in facing family hardship.
summary: Reconnected deeply with her brother over shared grief and childhood memories.
Felt significantly less alone after talking with Daniel.

quotes.text: We laughed. We haven't laughed together in years.

nodes.label: Autonomy and Personal Time
nodes.description: Needing space and time that belongs entirely to oneself.
summary: Claimed every other Saturday as her own day without caregiving duties.
Signed up for a pottery class to pursue personal interests.

nodes.label: Family and Loyalty
nodes.description: Deep commitment to caring for aging parents and supporting relatives.
summary: Committed to loving her mother even through memory loss and decline.
Collaborated with her brother to share caregiving responsibilities.

quotes.text: And I'll still have to love her like she's my mom.

nodes.label: Honesty and Authenticity
nodes.description: Valuing truthfulness in relationships and self-reflection.
summary: Confessed openly about her heavy drinking night without lying to the therapist.
Spoke her honest feelings directly to her brother.

quotes.text: I'm not going to lie to you.

edges.explanation: Believing her pain would burden others reinforced her pattern of handling everything alone.
Reaching out to her brother directly challenges and breaks her narrative of solitary caregiving.
Drinking heavily was a way to cope with the overwhelming isolation of the caregiving narrative.
Taking walks provided an adaptive alternative to carry the weight previously held alone.
Her lingering anger is closely intertwined with the painful grief of losing her mother.
She used wine as an escape from the unbearable reality defined by anticipatory loss.
Resting and sleeping well directly counteract the burnout of the selfless caregiver narrative.
Gaining connection with Daniel directly alleviates the isolation of the lone caregiver narrative.
Reclaiming Saturdays for herself helps dismantle the narrative that her life belongs entirely to her mother.
Her deep commitment to her mother makes the anticipatory grief all the more profound.
Honesty with her therapist and brother allowed her to release hidden anger and find relief.
